requirement:
> `Read a graph node by ID, source address, or node data. Returns text and, when more remains, a next UUID. A
> delivered page records its enclosing node.`
rationale:
structural: The requirement text is the exact description string for the `read_node` MCP tool. The only structural obligation is that the tool definition carries that description. `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tools.rs#impl[GraphSession<'_, '_, D>/Conversation]/fn[tools]` builds the `read_node` definition with a description identical to the requirement text. A search found no other definition of this description in the source. The review root covers the obligation. No other structural obligation (library, type, signature or delegation) is stated.

behavioral: The subject `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_node.mcp.description` fixes one thing: the description string of the `read_node` MCP tool. It has no `{test}` edges, and I found no test that checks this string.

The only source that carries it out is `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tools.rs#impl[GraphSession<'_, '_, D>/Conversation]/fn[tools]`. It puts the text in as a fixed string literal inside a `json!` tool definition. No condition or transformation touches that literal. The conditionals in `tools` concern the submission tool, extra tools and duplicate names, not the `read_node` description. This is the passed-through-unchanged case, so there is no branching or computation for a test to exercise. The requirement does not say a value must stay unchanged or distinct, so that exception does not apply.

The requirement states no other behavioral obligation, such as a MUST on runtime behavior or a boundary case. What the tool actually does when called belongs to other requirements. I therefore see no missing test obligation here.

The literal could contain a typo, and no test would catch it. I did not treat that as a gap, because there is no logic to verify.
